title: "Marker analysis — Ki-67 and CD3 per-cell rates"
output: html_document
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(glmmTMB)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

Six per-cell rate models: Ki-67 and CD3, each decomposed into the insulin,
glucagon and acinar bins. Each is a negative binomial mixed model with
`offset(log(count of the relevant cell type))`, so coefficients are rate ratios
**per cell of that type** rather than counts per islet.

Companion question: total endocrine cellularity per islet is preserved in T1D
despite near-complete beta-cell loss. These models ask whether proliferation
explains it; the selection test at the end asks whether survivor bias does.

## What is trustworthy, and what is not

**Verified** — computed from `fixef()` and `vcov()` or straight from the data,
and cross-checked against observed rates:

- the composition and denominator table
- the marginal Diagnosis effects from `marker_effects.R`
- the donor-level points and violins in every plot
- the survivor-selection test, which uses only `ratio_data` and `density_data`

- the Excel workbooks, which no longer use emmeans at all

`generate_marker_excel.R` has been rebuilt. Every marginal rate, group
difference and age slope is now an exact linear contrast of the fixed effects —
`estimate = l'beta`, `SE = sqrt(l' V l)` — so no transformations are composed
and each number can be checked by hand from the coefficient table. It refuses
to write any file until `validate_marker_rates()` passes.

The previous version routed those blocks through
`emmeans` → `regrid(transform = "log")` → `contrast(type = "response")` and
returned 4.64–4.99% for all six outcomes, including 4.70% for Ki-67 in alpha
cells where the observed rate is 0.62%. If you have workbooks from before this
rewrite, delete them.

**Still outstanding** — the stars on the Region, Sex and interaction panels of
the all-comparisons plots, which are suppressed by `SHOW_UNVERIFIED_STARS`; and
the count (abundance) workbooks, which need the same treatment applied to the
count formula.

```{r flags}
RUN_EXCEL <- TRUE    # rebuilt on exact linear contrasts; self-validating
RUN_PLOTS <- TRUE    # donor-level panels; see the note in that chunk
```

# 1. Preflight

```{r preflight}
source("Marker/R/marker_common.R")
source("Marker/R/marker_effects.R")
marker_preflight()
```

# 2. Data and denominators

```{r load}
# Single-stain runs are excluded: they detect insulin only, so Count.glu is
# structurally zero. Matches the exclusion already applied to ratio_data.
raw <- load_marker_data()
for (tag in names(raw)) {
  d <- raw[[tag]]
  cat(sprintf("%-5s %7d islets, %2d donors (ND %d / T1D %d)\n", tag, nrow(d),
              dplyr::n_distinct(d$Donor),
              dplyr::n_distinct(d$Donor[d$Diagnosis == "ND"]),
              dplyr::n_distinct(d$Donor[d$Diagnosis == "T1D"])))
}
```

```{r denominators}
# The numbers every rate is built on, and the paper's central observation:
# beta cells fall by about 31 per islet while alpha cells rise by about 33,
# leaving total cellularity per islet unchanged.
bind_rows(lapply(names(raw), function(tag) raw[[tag]] %>% mutate(marker = tag))) %>%
  group_by(marker, Diagnosis) %>%
  summarise(islets = n(), donors = dplyr::n_distinct(Donor),
            Islet.Cells = mean(Islet.Cells),
            Count.ins = mean(Count.ins), Count.glu = mean(Count.glu),
            Count.Acinar = mean(Count.Acinar), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 4)
```

# 3. Marginal effects, with the validation gate

```{r effects}
# Exact linear contrast on the coefficients: the T1D-vs-ND log rate ratio
# averaged with equal weights over the three regions and two sexes. No emmeans.
effects <- marker_effects_table()

# Hard stop if any model-derived ratio disagrees with the crude ratio by more
# than 3x. This is the check that would have caught the emmeans failure before
# it reached a figure.
validate_marker_rates(effects)
```

```{r effects-report}
cat("\n=== FIGURE AND LEGEND NUMBERS ===\n")
cat("Quote obs_ND / obs_T1D as the descriptive percentages — they are what the\n")
cat("figure's points show and need no back-transformation. Quote ratio, lwr,\n")
cat("upr and p from the model. Stars come from the sig column.\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(effects %>%
  dplyr::select(marker, cell, obs_ND, obs_T1D, ratio, lwr, upr, pct_change,
                p, sig, n_ND, n_T1D)), digits = 4)

cat("\n=== zero-inflation (reported separately, not in the CI above) ===\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(effects %>%
  dplyr::select(marker, cell, family, zi_ND, zi_T1D, zi_scale,
                marginal_ratio)), digits = 4)

dir.create("Marker/Results", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
readr::write_csv(effects, "Marker/Results/marker_effects.csv")
cat("\nSaved Marker/Results/marker_effects.csv\n")
```

# 4. Survivor-selection test

```{r selection}
# Independent of everything above: uses only ratio_data and density_data from
# the count pipeline. Falsifies pure survivor selection — alpha cells per mm2
# of tissue more than double, and selection can only remove cells.
source("Marker/R/plot_selection_figures.R")
sel_data <- prepare_selection_data()
sel_main <- generate_selection_main(sel_data)
sel_supp <- generate_selection_supp(sel_data)
```

# 5. Plots

```{r plots, eval = RUN_PLOTS}
# Donor-level violins and points are computed directly from the data and are
# correct. The STARS on the Region, Sex and interaction panels still come from
# the emmeans path and should not be reported until that is fixed. The
# Diagnosis panel stars should be checked against the sig column in section 3.
source("Marker/R/plot_marker_main_figure.R")
main <- generate_marker_main_figure()

source("Marker/R/plot_marker_all_comparisons.R")
generate_all_marker_plots()
```

# 6. Excel workbooks

```{r excel, eval = RUN_EXCEL}
# Validates all six Diagnosis contrasts against the observed rates and stops
# before writing if any disagree. On the Diagnosis sheet, rate_population
# should land near rate_observed and rate_median_donor should sit below both —
# the gap is the random-effect Jensen factor, reported on the Model Summary
# sheet.
source("Marker/R/generate_marker_excel.R")
generate_all_marker_excel()
```

```{r}
source("Marker/R/marker_sensitivity.R")
run_marker_sensitivity()      # both sensitivities on the four figure panels

```
